summary.title: Writing a C Compiler, Part 4
summary.one_liner: You learn how to add relational, equality, and short-circuit logical operators to a C compiler's parser and x86 code generator, using conditional set and jump instructions.
takeaways: Extend the grammar with one production rule per precedence level, e.g. logical-or, logical-and, equality, relational, additive.
Implement == and other relational operators by comparing two evaluated operands with cmpl and a conditional set instruction such as sete or setl.
Use the sign flag (SF) via setl-style instructions to determine ordering, since the zero flag only tests equality.
Implement && and || with short-circuit evaluation by emitting conditional jumps (je, jne) and jmp to unique labels.
summary.summary: This fourth part of Nora Sandler's series on writing a C compiler adds the logical operators && and || and the relational operators ==, !=, <, <=, >, and >=. It walks through updating the lexer with new tokens, extending the recursive-descent grammar with one rule per precedence level, and building the AST. Code generation covers emitting cmpl with conditional set instructions for comparisons, and conditional and unconditional jumps for short-circuit evaluation, with unique label generation. The article is a weekly assignment with accompanying tests and suggests optional extras such as modulo and bitwise operators.
